Unlike doctrine-registry.json / stack-registry.json / position-registry.json / authority-index.json, this file is not a pure deterministic text-extraction projection: implementation state is a judgment call that requires running real checks, not parsing prose. Structural completeness (every SCC-01..27 and V01..18 present exactly once, states drawn from the fixed enum) is itself verified by scripts/gate.ts's control-map-completeness step. See governance/PHASE_3A_KERNEL_REPORT.md for full Phase 3A evidence detail.
policy: A control is never 'implemented' merely because a document describes it; implementation requires an executable check.
A critical executable control requires at least one red fixture proving the gate actually fails on a real injected violation.
Absence of application/database/frontend code is represented honestly as not-yet-built, not as a passing or skipped control.
'partial' means a real, currently-passing executable check exists but does not yet cover the full required scope; the gap is named in notes.

evidence: packages/time/src/{instant,civil-date,as-of,clock,system-clock}.ts: Instant (absolute UTC instant, unambiguous canonical RFC 3339 string), CivilDate (separate YYYY-MM-DD type, no hidden timezone conversion), AsOf (requires BOTH businessAsOf and knowledgeAsOf — compile-time proven non-optional by tests/type-invalid/asof-missing-*.ts), and an explicit Clock capability with no package-owned ambient clock

scripts/check-architecture.ts's ambient-authoritative-time detector: mechanically enforces 'no implicit new Date()/Date.now() inside authoritative functions' across packages/*/src, allow-listing only the one explicitly named packages/time/src/system-clock.ts adapter
packages/time/tests/time.property.test.ts (fast-check): Instant and CivilDate canonical round-trip verified across a wide generated range
red_fixtures: Phase 3A red.ts runArchitectureFixtures() ambient-clock fixture (see SCC-24)
tests/type-invalid/asof-missing-business-boundary.ts + asof-missing-knowledge-boundary.ts (delegated into `pnpm red`)
doctrine_verification_controls.notes: PARTIAL, as the phase brief explicitly anticipates ('V10 covers temporal governance broadly. Time primitives alone are not full implementation.'). What exists: the primitives themselves, the bitemporal AsOf shape, the explicit-Clock discipline, and a real static control proving the ambient-time prohibition is mechanically enforced, not just documented. What does NOT exist: any actual business logic governed by these primitives (effective-dating rules, replay, as-of query resolution against real data) — TIM-01/TIM-02 full qualification requires that governed behavior to exist first.
doctrine_verification_controls.revisit_trigger: When a domain package exists that actually resolves AsOf-governed facts against stored data.

doctrine_verification_controls.title: Mutation sensitivity
evidence: Identical to SCC-18's evidence: two real, executed mutation-kill fixtures against packages/money/src domain-critical guards, proven via the real Vitest suite, not a mock.
red_fixtures: See SCC-18.
doctrine_verification_controls.notes: PARTIAL: two hand-picked domain-critical guards are proven mutation-sensitive by executed evidence, which is a genuine (if narrow) instance of GOV-03's 'a critical executable control must demonstrably be able to fail'. This is not a domain-wide mutation testing corpus (no StrykerJS run exists) — see SCC-18 for the identical honest scope statement.

doctrine_verification_controls.title: Oracle diversity
evidence: packages/money/tests/oracles/rounding-oracle.ts: independentHalfEvenRoundOracle — a genuinely independent second calculation path for half-even rounding (magnitude-first-then-reapply-sign strategy), authored separately from and never calling packages/money/src/rounding.ts's production roundExactRateToMinorUnits
packages/money/tests/rounding.test.ts: explicit example-based agreement assertions between the production function and the independent oracle for positive/negative/tie cases

packages/money/tests/rounding.property.test.ts (fast-check): production-vs-oracle agreement verified across a wide generated range of exact rational inputs, plus a 'rounded result is always within 0.5 of the exact value' property

packages/money/tests/{money,rate,minor-units}.property.test.ts (fast-check): additional property coverage (round-trip, add/subtract inverse, normalization) that is not a line-for-line reproduction of the implementation
doctrine_verification_controls.notes: PARTIAL, as the phase brief explicitly anticipates ('Do not prematurely claim V13. ... If no sufficiently independent oracle exists: mark V13 not-yet-built/partial rather than pretending.'). What exists: exactly one critical calculation (half-even rounding) has a real, independently-authored second calculation path, cross-verified by both example and property tests. What does NOT exist: oracle diversity across other calculations (there are currently no other 'critical calculations' in packages/errors/time/money beyond rounding — addition/subtraction are exact by construction and do not need a second oracle the way an inexact rounding boundary does), and no red fixture yet proves the oracle-agreement check itself would fail if the production function regressed (a natural next mutation-kill fixture).
doctrine_verification_controls.revisit_trigger: When a second critical calculation requiring an independent oracle is introduced (e.g. FX rate conversion), or when a red fixture is added proving the oracle-agreement test itself turns red on a genuine rounding regression.

doctrine_verification_controls.title: Provenance and reproducibility
doctrine_verification_controls.gate: pnpm run gate:authority && pnpm run build:authority-registry (byte-identity) && pnpm run verify:toolchain
evidence: scripts/build-authority-registry.ts regenerates governance/*.json byte-identically from doctrine/DOCTRINE.md, stack/STACK.md, position/POSITION.md (DET-01/DET-02 satisfied for the governance-registry layer: deterministic compilation from committed definitions, not an AI authoring claim). Phase 2.1 note: the only byte-level change from the .mjs->.ts migration in any of the 4 generated registries is the disclosed "generated_by" provenance string (now points at the .ts filename); every extracted object, hash, and count is unchanged — verified with `git diff` immediately after migration.
scripts/check-authority-integrity.ts registry-drift checks are the executable red condition for 'hidden change without regeneration'

pnpm-lock.yaml + .node-version + package.json engines/packageManager give a real dependency/toolchain lock (contributes to GOV-05's 'complete verification bundle' requirement, which did not exist before Phase 2)

Phase 2.1: the toolchain-lock layer's own exactness was investigated more deeply (see SCC-04) and found to have a real gap (TypeScript-6 compatibility engine resolves via a transitive semver range to a patch different from the declared baseline) — this is additional, more precise evidence about the boundary of what is and is not yet provenance-proven, not a new capability

Phase 2.2: the toolchain-lock layer's reproducibility was independently verified, not just inspected — the TypeScript-6 engine resolution was reproduced from a from-scratch disposable install of only the exact declared package specifier, ruling out this-repository-local lockfile contamination as the cause. stack/VERSION_BASELINE.json was also completed with previously-absent pnpm/Turborepo reference patches, so the toolchain-lock layer's own DECLARED-vs-ACTUAL provenance surface (still governance-registry/toolchain-lock scope, not extended into the application layer) is now more completely covered than at end of Phase 2.1

Phase 3A: a first, narrow instance of application-layer determinism now exists and is real, not merely governance-registry provenance — packages/money/src/{minor-units,money}.ts define exactly one canonical textual form per value (DET-05: 'exactly one textual form is accepted/produced') for MinorUnits (integer string, leading zeros/'-0'/decimal/exponential all rejected) and Money (currency + minorUnits string pair), each proven by an explicit round-trip property test (packages/money/tests/money.property.test.ts). This is application-layer, not governance-registry, evidence — the first such evidence this control has had — but it covers only the money package's canonical-form invariant, not GOV-05's broader 'complete verification bundle' (still no CI execution, no application dependency graph beyond 3 packages, and the SCC-04 compat-engine gap is unchanged)
red_fixtures: check-authority-integrity.ts --self-test registry-drift-sensitive fixtures (alter rule_verbatim, omit V08, etc., plus Phase 2.1's new stack-seal/position-seal fixtures, all cause byte-identity/completeness to fail)
red:toolchain-mismatch (scripts/red.ts) for 'hidden toolchain change', plus Phase 2.2's 5 isolated single-component toolchain fixtures and the lockfile-disagreement fixture
doctrine_verification_controls.notes: Proven only for the governance-registry generation layer (doctrine/stack/position -> governance/*.json), the toolchain pin layer, and now (Phase 3A) one narrow application-layer canonical-form invariant. NOT proven for the application/financial system as a whole: there is no migration, ledger, or generator determinism to test yet, and GOV-05's 'complete verification bundle' is not yet fully assembled (no CI execution observed from this environment — confirmed in Phase 2.2 that no git remote is even configured here, not just that a run wasn't checked — no application dependency graph beyond 3 kernel packages, and the toolchain lock itself still has the SCC-04 compat-engine gap, now more precisely documented). Marking this V-control implemented for the whole doctrine would overstate reality; 'partial' remains the honest state. Phase 3A's addition is real but intentionally narrow (one invariant, one package) and does not by itself close the gap to 'implemented'.
doctrine_verification_controls.revisit_trigger: When application-layer generators (codegen, migrations) exist and can be shown to regenerate byte-identically with a red fixture for hidden toolchain change at that layer too, and when the SCC-04 compat-engine gap is closed.
